review.brief: Review the whole of RM29 tier 3 (diff range 5952a23..HEAD, ignore progress.json churn). Validate, in order: (1) module boundaries - analytics now owns its OWN database; confirm no module reads another module's DB, cross-module data flows only through public Go interfaces (telemetry/charging updated-since read ports), the gateway calls interfaces and never a database, and no HTML escapes internal/gateway. (2) Every DB object matches the user-confirmed design: design.md 'Database Changes' (vehicle_metrics, vehicle_metric_watermarks) and its Index Plan, plus D1-D9. Any schema/index/constraint that differs from the confirmed design is a BLOCKER finding, however sensible the deviation looks. (3) The integration tests in internal/analytics/db_integration_test.go assert design.md's up-front Test Contract (Fixtures A/B/C + the Reconcile idempotence contract, design.md lines 639-788) - not whatever the implementation happens to produce. A test whose expected value was clearly read off the code is a finding. (4) Doc-pack conventions: display-unit suffixes on every persisted unit-bearing column and domain field with conversion on write not read; bilingual i18n for any user-facing gateway string; docs-track-change (README structure/architecture, module AGENTS.md/README) updated in THIS change. (5) Performance-Profile compliance - the precomputed read model and its indexes must be justified against the declared read patterns. (6) Look hard at three known-fragile spots: D5's recalculate-after-write wiring (a nil AnalyticsRecalculator in cmd/web slipped past every automated signal and was fixed late as task 5.6 - check EVERY construction site, not just the fixed one), D4's 24h commit-skew overlap guard, and D13's rule that ConsumedByDay/OdometerDeltaByDay are SELECT+map+NOT-NULL-filter with NO derivation logic left in them. (7) Anti-gaming: acceptance criteria and tasks are append-only - flag any weakened or deleted criterion, any status a worker self-approved, and any design decision the implementation quietly reinterpreted. Test signals: assistant-run were go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l, make build/vet/bins, make ui-guard/i18n-guard/money-guard, openspec validate --strict (all green). User-reported were make migrate-up, the full go test suite, and the one-off backfill run (all green, the owner's report). You must judge test QUALITY by reading the tests - never run the suite yourself.

findings.note: cmd/poller/main.go never constructs analytics.NewRecalculator and never calls Recalculator.Reconcile anywhere in production code (confirmed: grep -rn "\.Reconcile(" --include="*.go" . | grep -v _test.go returns zero hits repo-wide). The diff to cmd/poller/main.go is exactly one line (the new leading pool arg to analytics.NewReader, line 88) -- the rest of task 5.5 ("Construct analytics.NewRecalculator(...) alongside the existing analyticsReader. Add a per-vehicle Reconcile call...") was never done. This is not a minor omission: the proposal's own 'What Changes' section states 'cmd/poller gains a per-vehicle Reconcile call after each successful collection cycle' as an in-scope item (not listed under 'Out of scope'), design.md's Rollout note assumes Reconcile 'runs nightly thereafter' by 'the same code path', and internal/gateway/handlers/charges.go's own new doc comment on recalculateAfterChargeWrite says the chart 'falls back to the last-recalculated state until the next nightly Reconcile call heals it (design.md D7)' -- a guarantee the shipped code does not honor. specs/analytics/spec.md's 'Incremental Recompute Via An Analytics-Owned Watermark' requirement (ADDED, not deferred) is consequently unimplemented in production. Concrete failure: after this change ships, the nightly poller keeps writing new vehicle_snapshots and supercharger_sessions rows as always, but nothing ever calls Reconcile to propagate them into vehicle_metrics. Since ConsumedByDay/OdometerDeltaByDay now read EXCLUSIVELY from vehicle_metrics (D-precompute), every vehicle's odometer and battery-consumed dashboard charts will silently stop advancing past the one-time backfill date (task 8.2, run via a throwaway script since deleted) for any day not touched by a manual charge-entry write -- a severe, user-visible regression that directly contradicts this change's own D10 characterization bar ('pin current output, assert identical after the move'). tasks.md correctly leaves task 5.5 unchecked ([ ]), which per ai/agentic-workflow.md ('tasks.md wins on implementation done-ness') means this tier's own artifacts already know it is incomplete -- but progress.json's rollup.done lists '5.5' as done, task '5.5' status is 'done' with note 'same one-line call-site fix', and top-level status is 'verified', which is inconsistent with the actual code and should not have reached review as ready-to-archive. Fix: cmd/poller/main.go must construct analytics.NewRecalculator(pool, telemetry.NewReader(pool), telemetry.NewSuperchargerReader(pool), charging.NewReader(pool)) and add a per-vehicle Reconcile(ctx, v.AccountID, v.TeslaID) call after each successful collection cycle, mirroring newGapReconciler's existing shape, exactly as task 5.5 and the proposal's 'What Changes' section require.

findings.note: RE-VERIFIED FIXED in commit 10c08cf. cmd/poller/main.go now hoists telemetryReader/superchargerReader/chargingReader into shared locals, constructs analytics.NewRecalculator(pool, telemetryReader, superchargerReader, chargingReader), and newNightlyReconciler (renamed from newGapReconciler) calls recalculator.Reconcile(ctx, v.AccountID, v.TeslaID) as step 1 for every registered vehicle, before the existing ConsumedByDay + gapWriter.ReconcileWindow step 2. `grep -rn "\.Reconcile(" --include="*.go" . | grep -v _test.go` now finds the one production call site (cmd/poller/main.go). go build ./..., go vet ./cmd/poller/... ./internal/analytics/..., and gofmt -l cmd/poller/main.go all clean, confirmed directly. tasks.md 5.5 correctly flipped [ ] -> [x] (no other task/criterion text touched). Ordering claim verified against telemetry.AGENTS.md's GapWriter contract and gap_writer.go's actual ReconcileWindow implementation (read directly, lines 63-103): ConsumedByDay is a pure SELECT over vehicle_metrics per D13 (confirmed in round 1), so running the gap step before Reconcile would compute `flagged` from yesterday's model and never see the night's just-collected snapshot -- the reordering is a correctness fix, not a style preference, and correctly supersedes task 5.5's stale 'two independent calls' framing (a design fact this tier's own change made true, not a re-litigation of anything reviewed in round 1). Placement is still entirely inside reconcilingCollector.CollectAll, gated on c.inner.CollectAll(ctx) succeeding first, so RM28 D4 ('after snapshots are written' -- confirmed against openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-16-RM28-battery-derive-consumed-per-day/design.md:537) is satisfied for both halves, not just the gap half. Skip-on-failure claim verified against ReconcileWindow's real code: it DELETEs every existing charge_gaps row in [start,end] absent from the freshly-computed `flagged` set (gap_writer.go:99-103), so running step 2 on a vehicle whose Reconcile just failed would compute `flagged` from stale vehicle_metrics and delete real, still-outstanding gap rows -- skip-then-self-heal-next-cycle is correct, fall-through would destroy state. Per-vehicle isolation preserved: `continue` on a Reconcile error only advances the `for _, v := range vehicles` loop to the next vehicle, mirroring CollectAll's own existing isolation pattern; one vehicle's Reconcile failure cannot abort another vehicle's reconciliation. Docs: cmd/README.md's cmd/poller row now states the order and why it's required; internal/analytics/AGENTS.md's Reconcile bullet now states cmd/poller is Reconcile's only production caller, when it runs relative to the gap step, and what breaks if the call is dropped -- both accurate against the shipped code, both sufficient for a future agent to rediscover this without re-deriving it from source.

decisions.decision: IO-1 grain/PK: vehicle-day, UUID PK + UNIQUE(account_id,tesla_id,metric_date)
decisions.why: Matches vehicle_snapshots' deduped daily grain and charge_gaps' precedent. A per-snapshot FK into telemetry was rejected as a module-boundary violation.

decisions.decision: IO-2 watermark in a dedicated cursor table, not a column on vehicle_metrics
decisions.why: Survives the zero-rows first run; MAX() over the metrics table would silently rewind when a row is recomputed away.

decisions.decision: IO-3 one cursor row per (vehicle, source), three sources
decisions.why: manual_charge_entries is user-edited at any hour while the other two move at midnight; one shared cursor couples those clocks.

decisions.decision: IO-4 commit-skew guard: 24h safety overlap on the cursor read
decisions.why: Without it a user edit landing mid-run is skipped permanently and silently. UPSERT is idempotent so re-reads are free.

decisions.decision: IO-5 Recalculate after the manual-charge write
decisions.why: That chart updates instantly today; precomputing without this ships a user-visible regression against D10's characterization bar.

decisions.decision: IO-6 only snapshot-derived math leaves the gateway; Supercharger tiles defer to T6
decisions.why: T6 moves those session rows to charging anyway - doing them here writes the same code twice.

decisions.decision: Design gate: schema approved with one revision - dense table, nullable _calc + consumed_pct
decisions.why: Sparse rows meant a vehicle's first day had no row, so re-pointing the battery chart later would silently drop day 1.

decisions.decision: consumed_pct nullable with flagged=false on predecessor-less rows; both Reader queries filter IS NOT NULL
decisions.why: Necessary consequence of the owner's dense-table call: a stored 0 would make every vehicle's first day masquerade as a charge gap, and unfiltered reads would change ConsumedByDay's output.

decisions.decision: Wave 1 dispatched as TWO parallel workers (telemetry 1.1-1.3, charging 1.4) rather than one serial worker
decisions.why: A worker is sandboxed to one module, so a single serial dispatch is impossible here. Disjoint modules, 5h bucket at 26%, and wave 1 gates all seven remaining waves.

decisions.decision: Left internal/gateway/handlers/handlers_test.go gofmt-unclean
decisions.why: Verified against HEAD via git stash: it was already unformatted before this change. Same call as tier 2's D6 - gofmt only what the change churns, or the tier widens.

decisions.decision: Appended task 2.5 to wire Makefile MIGRATIONS_DIRS and .air.toml, rather than editing task 2.4
decisions.why: No original task covered it. sqlc reads sqlc.yaml directly, so codegen and build stay green while migrate-up never applies the analytics migrations. Tasks are append-only.

decisions.decision: Pulled tasks 5.4/5.5 forward from Wave 5 into the Wave 3 boundary
decisions.why: NewReader's signature change broke the repo build at both cmd/ call sites. Leaving it broken across Waves 4-6 would suppress go vet - the one cheap signal covering unexecuted tests.

decisions.decision: Accepted the worker's UTC 'yesterday' clamp in Reconcile rather than adding a *time.Location parameter
decisions.why: The poller runs at local midnight, where UTC and Bogota yesterday agree; only evening manual reruns diverge, and D4's 24h overlap self-heals that. Widening the port would reopen the gated interface.

decisions.decision: Accepted the removal of five reader tests, but appended task 6.4 to re-assert their behaviours against Recalculate
decisions.why: Verified ConsumedByDay no longer calls the ports, so the tests asserted a deleted path. Removal alone would have silently dropped fetch-window, scoping and error-propagation coverage.

decisions.decision: Left the mis-scoped commit 4603172 in place instead of rewriting history
decisions.why: The gateway worker was still writing to those files. A soft reset or amend mid-write risks capturing a torn state; an accurate follow-up commit costs nothing and keeps the record honest.

decisions.decision: Leader finished the interrupted gateway task in-session rather than re-dispatching a fresh worker
decisions.why: The work was nearly complete and its remaining state was diagnosable from git diff plus vet. A cold re-dispatch would re-read the doc pack and risk redoing finished edits.

decisions.decision: Fixed the three failing tests rather than the implementation
decisions.why: design.md's Test Contract is authoritative and its expected values were already correct; the fixtures mis-transcribed the INPUTS. Changing the code to match a wrong fixture would have broken real behaviour.

decisions.decision: Escalated Wave 6's cross-module fixture gap to the owner instead of picking a fix on autopilot
decisions.why: Every fix adds shared test infrastructure or new public surface in modules this change does not own, and binds tiers 5-7 too. Outside the roadmap Decisions.

decisions.decision: Unblock 6.1-6.3 with a multi-dir testdb harness (os.DirFS over sibling migration dirs) plus direct-SQL fixture seeding
decisions.why: Owner chose it over exporting test-only writers from telemetry (new public surface in tier 4's module) and over deferring the DB proofs that tier 4's column drop rests on.

decisions.decision: Applied each migration dir with its own goose provider instead of merging them into one union FS
decisions.why: account and charging both ship version 20260720000001; a merged FS dies on the collision. Per-dir sequencing is also exactly what the Makefile's migrate-up loop already does.

decisions.decision: gofmt -w'd the two branch-touched unclean files, reversing D10's deferral; left the 8 pre-existing ones alone
decisions.why: D10 deferred handlers_test.go only because a worker was writing it live. Nothing is live now, and task 8.1 expects gofmt clean. The other 8 predate this branch and are out of scope.

decisions.decision: Appended task 5.6 and fixed the nil AnalyticsRecalculator myself rather than reopening Wave 5 or leaving it for the reviewer
decisions.why: Waves 5's tasks are closed and owner-verified, so they are not reopenable. Catching it at this gate costs one commit; catching it in review costs a rework wave plus a re-review.

decisions.what: Amend the tip commit to remove the accidentally committed 15MB backfill binary, rather than adding a follow-up delete commit.
decisions.why: Branch has no upstream and nobody else holds it, so amending keeps the 15MB out of git history entirely; a delete commit would leave it in every future clone.

decisions.what: Run Reconcile BEFORE the charge-gap step in the same per-vehicle loop, and skip a vehicle's gap step entirely when its Reconcile fails.
decisions.why: Task 5.5 called the two calls independent; they no longer are. ConsumedByDay is now a SELECT over vehicle_metrics (D13), so gaps computed before Reconcile read yesterday's model, and ReconcileWindow would DELETE gap flags on stale evidence.

decisions.what: Rename newGapReconciler to newNightlyReconciler and hoist the three sibling ports into shared locals.
decisions.why: The step now has two halves, so the old name actively misleads; the ports are stateless handles over one pool, and building them twice would hide that both halves read identical sources. No callers outside the file.
